title: Why AI Agents Still Won't Pay for Anything — Jan Curn, Apify
talk_summary: Jan Curn argues agentic payment protocols have near-zero adoption because agents already use pre-provisioned API keys, setup/trust friction is high, and token subsidies remove incentives to buy services. He frames adoption as a funnel—need, setup, discovery, purchase—and predicts progress when always-on agents get budgets, trusted directories mature, and variable pay-per-use settlement works.

takeaways.technique: Pre-provisioned API keys over agentic payments
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents access external services through fixed accounts, API keys, or MCP connectors rather than autonomous per-call payment wallets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they are competing with with API keys because it's just the more convenient way

takeaways.technique: Internal token budgets to force build-vs-buy
takeaways.what_they_do: Token subsidies make agents build from scratch because marginal token cost feels free; exposing real costs changes the build-vs-buy decision.
takeaways.evidence_quote: on $100 per month on claude you can buy I don't know like $14,000 worth of tokens if you max it out
takeaways.numbers: $100/month Claude subscription can buy ~$14,000 worth of tokens if maxed out

takeaways.what_they_do: Use curated directories or marketplaces with verified connectors so agents can trust which services to call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: cloth uh has uh has a directory of connectors right it's like sort of like verified connectors

takeaways.what_they_do: Give agents small budgets first, then increase them only after successful runs prove trust.
